blocks.etymology: From Middle English scren, screne (“windscreen, firescreen”), from Anglo-Norman escren (“firescreen, the tester of a bed”), Old French escren, escrein, escran (modern French écran (“screen”)), from Middle Dutch scherm, from Old Dutch skirm, from Proto-West Germanic *skirmi, from Proto-Germanic *skirmiz (“fur, shelter, covering, screen”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ker- (“to cut, divide”). senses.definition: The flat glass surface on a computer, television, or phone where pictures and words are shown.

examples.en: He spent the whole afternoon staring at his computer screen.

senses.definition: A large flat surface in a cinema where films are projected for people to watch.

senses.definition: A piece of furniture or light wall used to divide a room or hide something.
